analysis:
Examined the MTP upgrade head text (ProviderLoop+MTPUpgrade.swift) and the ModelLoading patch and base text. The changes are scheduling and availability bookkeeping. They do not touch encryption, attestation, authorization or the cache key derivation.

(1) Load-transition generations. transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) was added at MTPUpgrade.swift:127 and at ModelLoading head :397 and :434 (the :434 call carries subject: modelId). It is a generation bump with no visible end call. The semantics of the transitionGenerations type are not supplied. Integration should confirm the bump is used only for invalidation of stale snapshots, such as cached capacity or the heartbeat. It must not gate any authorization state (TB-011/T-053).

(2) Autopilot load guard. At head :207, autopilotAllowsModel was replaced by autopilotServesModel. Neither definition is supplied, so whether the new predicate narrows or widens which models may load is unverified. This is availability and policy only; there is no consumer-data impact.

(3) Unload reconciliation. reconcileAutopilotPlacements() is now called after a slot is removed (head :1148-1150). This is consistent with the comment that a request must not reload an adopted model under an Autopilot placement.

(4) Eviction snapshot. evictableModelSlots now excludes slots held by Autopilot (autopilotHoldsModel). This is an availability change. It could cause more 503 'slot' errors when every slot is held, but the existing T-016/T-029 DoS class covers that.

On T-041, the MTP replacement preserves original.cacheEligibleWeightHash and modelArtifactSHA256 (MTPUpgrade.swift:171-172 and :237-238), so SSD cache binding to the verified weight hash is unchanged. The weight-hash capture and publication paths in the base text are unchanged.

No regression was identified. Remaining questions are the transitionGenerations consumers and the autopilotServesModel semantics.
